The corpus naming trap holds here as everywhere: the checker's version number is its own, not its subject's. check-c2-v12.py checks v11; so does its predecessor check-c2-v11.py -- v12 is a successor instrument over the SAME subject bytes, written because freeze section 7.2 forbids editing the reviewed check-c2-v11.py.

advisories.title: The effective checker cannot run to completion on the live tree: its pinned input check-completeness.py has moved (freeze section 7.8.1 class, refusal side)
advisories.detail: check-c2-v12.py PINS check-completeness.py at 6c52a5f9a4ac6a3ec3dae9fb0c87e82552744b18eb8cc38d1c4522ade3e549d6 (the docs-init bytes, git 7cc0f8a). The live tree carries af9f8837a5abc561cefebf071b862e2dd5fb427304f4738f7fadf5872c4f0f1f, committed by c06eaea 'Instrument dialect repair' in the active coordinator lane. Measured this run: python3 -I -B artifacts/check-c2-v12.py exits 2 printing 'C2V12-REFUSED: pinned input check-completeness.py: declared 6c52a5f9..., measured af9f8837...'. Per section 7.8.1 this refusal is the CORRECT behavior -- loud, named, scoped to exit 2 exactly as the instrument's checkerModeContract declares, and it must NEVER be read as a substantive verdict about c2-plan-stage-schema.v11.json. But operationally C-2's register-named validator cannot go green on the live corpus until the coordinator reconciles. Note the artifact side too: v11's own recordedInputs[4] publishes the OLD digest 6c52a5f9... for artifacts/check-completeness.py, so even a re-pinned successor checker would fire C2V12-RECORDED-INPUT against v11's published digest table on the live tree. This is the freeze section 7.9 class again -- the dialect repair moved a file that both C-2's head artifact and its validator pin -- and reconciling it is a coordinator act, not a patch.

advisories.title: The instrument's authority prose and one of its binds encode the pre-application state
advisories.detail: The docstring AUTHORITY section and the green-run banner state 'c2-plan-stage-schema.v9 remains the head and check-c2-v9.py remains its instrument'. True when the file was written; stale since the 2026-08-05 application recorded in freeze section 1.1 (head v11, validator check-c2-v12.py). Separately, L12 binds the resolved effective contract's checkerModeContract.checker to the literal 'check-c2-v9.py' -- faithfully enforcing what the reviewed v11 bytes actually say (the freeze row records this same stale pointer as carried-forward finding (1) and forbids patching it under section 7.2). Consequence for the coordinator: any future successor contract that repairs checkerModeContract.checker to name the real validator will be refused by THIS instrument by design, so that repair necessarily ships with a successor instrument.

advisories.title: Blanket refusal where a named skip would preserve coverage (freeze section 7.8.1 rule 2)
advisories.detail: The moved check-completeness.py pin feeds only L3's second-resolver cross-check, yet its drift refuses the entire run at exit 2; the other gates, which do not depend on it, lose their coverage. Section 7.8.1 rule 2 prefers a scoped, named skip at a distinct exit code for a per-class input. The choice is declared in the instrument's exit contract and is fail-closed, so it is a design note, not a defect.

advisories.detail: Verified by attack: replacing knownLimitations[0] with 'This instrument IS independent review and a green run IS product acceptance' runs at exit 0, FINDINGS: 0. whatWasTested.sourceReadInFull: All 3095 lines. Key disciplines verified in source and by execution: subject hash-verified before parse (exit 2 on drift); every pinned input hash-verified before parse or module-exec; duplicate JSON keys refused and NAMED at their key via object_pairs_hook; law 18 by identity test (value is True or value is False) BEFORE the int test in jtype, and type-exact comparison (type(left) is not type(right)) in exact_equal, so bool-for-int and int-for-bool both fire; os never imported, no directory enumeration primitive anywhere in the file; declared paths admitted only through SAFE_REL_RE with '..' refused.
whatWasTested.derivationResolution: resolve() locates the derivation declaration BY SHAPE (one filename, one sha256, one operation list inside a top-level object) rather than by the key name 'derivedFrom' -- the CMP-IR-01 discipline; refuses ambiguity (two derivation-shaped objects: measured refusal 'ambiguous derivation: derivedFrom, secondDeclaration'); hash-verifies each predecessor against BOTH the instrument's PINS and the declaration's own sha256 before parsing; requires every 'set' to restate type-exactly the value it replaces (measured: from=True where predecessor holds int 10 refuses at exit 2) and every 'add' to land on a fresh object member; recursion guards revisits. The materialised effective contract is cross-checked type-exactly against check-completeness.py's independent resolver (L3 'second resolver: check-completeness.py agrees, type-exact'). It resolves by value shape with digest verification; it does not read the delta flat.
